rules.statement: A deed of gift does not create a fidei commissum if it only prohibits alienation and does not clearly designate the party or parties who are to take the property after the donees.
rules.supporting_quote: "The question is whether there is a clear designation of those who are to take the property after the death of the immediate donees. The District Judge thinks that in the above passage 'the executors, administrators, and assigns' are those of the descendants of the donees and not of the donees themselves, and that the fidei commissum varies are the descendants. But this is an impossible construction. All the words 'descendants, executors, administrators, and assigns.' go together and clearly refer to the descendants, executors, administrators, and assigns of the donees."
